verdict: OK to lend in Faridabad auto components — pursue tier-2/tier-3 suppliers to Maruti and EV-linked programmes with tight covenants; avoid single-OEM, ICE-engine-only and unaudited workshops.
title: Faridabad Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Faridabad's auto cluster is a machining-and-assembly trade: castings, forgings, sheet metal, wiring and fluid-transmission parts bought by OEMs on schedule and paid weeks later.** Cash is consumed at the input end (metal, power, labour) and released only when the OEM approves the part and pays; value sits in the tooling and the approved-vendor status, not in the shed. Faridabad has carried this trade for generations — Imperial Auto was set up here in 1969 [2] — so the city has deep supplier depth but also old assets and old product lines. **The city's own auto news is thin: the local stories we hold are a workshop armouring-cars raid [1] and unregistered autos [3], neither of which tells us cluster health — so lean on first principles and peers here.**

## Where cash and value sit
**Working capital is the whole game: gross current assets averaged 160-170 days in recent years at a comparable component maker [10], so a supplier can be profitable and still short of cash.** Pricing power is real only where design complexity is high — diesel fuel injection is cited as an example of complexity that strengthens pricing power [11] — and weak in commodity fabrication. **So when a proposal lands, check the OEM-wise sales split and the tooling ownership; if one buyer is above half of sales, ask for the supply agreement and payment terms in writing.** Engine-and-related parts carry obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]; treat a pure ICE-engine book as a declining annuity, not a growth story.

## What has changed now
**Demand is running hot: IIP for NIC 29 output is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D], and Haryana GST is +10.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D].** Peers confirm the volume: Motherson Sumi Wiring revenue grew 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore with profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore [4], and Lumax lifted its growth outlook after a strong first half [7]. **But bank credit is +27.0% YoY against output +19.2%, a gap of +7.8 pp [D] — money is entering this chain faster than metal is leaving it, so some of what you will see is leverage, not demand.** Margins are the pressure point: aluminium is squeezing margins at ASK [5] and Q4FY26 earnings were expected strong on volumes with margins under pressure [6].

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2 and tier-3 suppliers with an approved-vendor code at a Maruti-tier OEM, a second customer line, and EV or lightweighting order wins of the kind ASK reports [5].** Avoid single-customer fabricators, workshops with no audited accounts, and anyone whose only edge is a labour contract. **Structure short: 12-month limits, monthly stock-and-debtor statements, and a covenant that Debt/EBITDA stays under 2.5-2.75 times — the level at which rating agencies flag weak cash generation [10].** Take the debtor ageing and the top-five customer list every month, and a quarterly CMA. **Price for the metal: ask for the hedging policy, because rating methodology weighs hedging against profits [8].**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the gap between sales growth and receivable days: if debtor days stretch while sales rise, the OEM is funding itself with your borrower's money.** Watch inventory of engine-specific parts — obsolescence risk is explicit in the rating criteria [11]. Watch any sudden capex for a single programme without a written nomination. **And watch the local enforcement stories: a raid like the armouring case [1] signals an unrecorded order book, so if a borrower's workshop is in that trade, ask for the job-card register.**
